gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold chief complaint is wheeze; generated chief complaint is increased shortness of breath. Wheeze is not explicitly captured.
Gold describes 2–3 days of wheeze; generated HPI describes 2–3 days of shortness of breath, not wheeze.
Gold states no fever and temp 37 °C; generated facts mention subjective fever but do not state absence of fever or the context of a normal 37 °C temperature.
Gold notes cold symptoms; generated set does not mention cold symptoms explicitly.
Gold: not coughing up sputum. Generated hpi-009: no sputum expectoration with cough – equivalent.

Gold: denies haemoptysis or chest pain. Generated has no haemoptysis (hpi-010) and no chest pain (hpi-007), but they are separated; the combined denial is not necessary to be preserved as one fact. Content is captured across two generated facts.
Gold: not waking at night because of symptoms. Generated hpi-008: no night-time wakening due to symptoms – same meaning.
Gold: currently not exercising. Generated facts note exercise intolerance and SOB on exertion but do not state that the patient is not exercising at present.
Gold: sometimes cannot complete sentences but no SOB at rest. Generated hpi-004 only captures difficulty finishing sentences when walking and does not mention that there is no SOB at rest.
Gold: no problems walking upstairs. Generated facts do not mention stairs.

Gold: more wheezy walking to work. Generated hpi-006: daytime SOB on exertion; this reflects worse breathing with exertion but does not explicitly mention wheeze or walking to work. The specific wheeze detail is not captured, so the exact gold fact is not fully covered.
Gold: does not have a peak-flow meter at home. Generated facts only state that a peak-flow meter will be prescribed; absence at baseline is not explicitly stated.
Gold: has missed a few days of work. No generated fact reports missed work.
Gold: history of asthma since childhood. Generated pmh-001: childhood and adult asthma – this includes and extends the gold but supports it.
Gold: hospital admissions for asthma but no ITU. Generated pmh-004: past hospital visits for asthma, and pmh-005: no ICU admission – together capture this.
Gold: hayfever. Generated pmh-002: hay fever – same condition.
Gold: eczema. Generated pmh-003: eczema – matches.
Gold: intermittently uses salbutamol every few weeks. Generated med-001: salbutamol inhaler used every few weeks historically – same pattern.
Gold: needs salbutamol when exercising. No generated fact states use specifically tied to exercise.
Gold: stopped regular asthma medication 3–4 years ago. Generated facts do not mention stopping regular meds or timing.
Gold: no known drug allergies. Generated allergy-001: no drug allergies reported – equivalent.
Gold: non-smoker. Generated sh-003: non-smoker – matches.
Gold: 1 unit alcohol every 2–3 days. Generated sh-004: about one glass of wine every 2–3 days – same quantity/frequency though phrased as a glass of wine.
Gold: lives with partner. Generated sh-001: lives with their partner – matches.
Gold: works as an engineer. Generated sh-002: works as an engineer – matches.
Gold: exacerbation of asthma. Generated asm-001: acute asthma exacerbation/asthma flare – same impression.

Gold: continue to monitor temperature and contact clinic if spiking temperatures. Generated facts do not mention ongoing temperature monitoring or spikes as a primary plan item (only mention earlier contact if fever increases in follow-up).

Gold: collect prescription for peak-flow meter and spacer. Generated plan-001 and plan-002: prescribe peak flow meter and spacer – functionally equivalent, though framed as prescription rather than collection.
Gold: pharmacist will advise how to use peak-flow meter and spacer. Generated plan-003: pharmacist to demonstrate spacer and peak flow technique – equivalent.
Gold: record PEFR twice daily on waking and at night. Generated plan-001: record PEF first thing and in evening daily for next week – essentially same instruction, with added duration.
Gold: increase salbutamol with spacer to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours. Generated plan-004: salbutamol 2–4 puffs every 4 hours – same regimen.
Gold: may need to add another inhaler. Generated plan does not mention adding a second inhaler in future.
Gold: advised to take regular antihistamine. Generated plan-005: recommends regular OTC antihistamine for hay fever – same core instruction.
Gold: arrange review next week. Generated fu-001: follow-up review in ~1 week – matches.

Gold: urgent appointment if wheeze not settling/worsening and feels unwell. Generated fu-002 mentions earlier contact if fever increases or wheeze worsens but omits the criterion of wheeze not settling and feeling unwell or specifying an urgent appointment.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold chief complaint is wheeze; generated chief complaint is increased SOB. SOB is not described as chief complaint in gold and is different from wheeze.
Gold notes 2–3 days of wheeze, not SOB. Worsening SOB over 2–3 days is not documented in gold.

Generated states associated cough; gold explicitly states not coughing up sputum and notes no cough (only cold symptoms) and no HPI cough documentation, and specifically cold symptoms with no cough up sputum. Presence of cough is not supported and conflicts with the absence of sputum-producing cough; conservative classification as contradiction as it introduces a symptom not suggested in gold.
Generated: subjective fever associated with SOB. Gold: no fever and temp 37 °C. Direct conflict.
Exercise intolerance is not mentioned in gold; gold instead states the patient is not exercising at the moment and has no problems walking upstairs.

Daytime SOB on exertion is not described in gold, which focuses on wheeze, occasional difficulty finishing sentences, and worse wheeze walking to work, but does not generalize to daytime SOB on exertion.
Gold specifies asthma since childhood. Generated extends to childhood and adult asthma; adult asthma component is additional but not conflicting.

Gold records temp 37 °C in HPI context; generated moves this into physical findings as patient-reported. Content (37 °C) is consistent with gold but section classification is different. As a fact, it is supported, but because there is no gold physical examination section, this is treated as an added structuring rather than a direct match.
Gold does not comment on whether there are other vitals or exam findings; stating that none are documented is an extra meta-comment.
Gold lists hayfever as PMH but does not explicitly assess allergic rhinitis as a comorbid contributor in the assessment section. This is a clinical inference/addition.

Gold follow-up and plan mention urgent appointment if wheeze not settling/getting worse and if unwell, but do not specify inability to speak in sentences or other concerning signs. These criteria are additional safety-net details.

Gold advises urgent appointment if wheeze not settling/worsening and feeling unwell, and separate advice to monitor temperature and speak to clinic if spiking temperatures. Generated compresses this to earlier contact if fever increases or wheeze worsens, omitting the 'not settling' and 'feels unwell' qualifiers. It partially overlaps but rephrases and simplifies, so treated as an addition rather than exact support.
